body_markdown:
###


Speak directly to the patient in short segments and preserve the screening tool's exact wording, timeframes, and response choices during the interpreted exchange. Clarify unfamiliar terms after the scored items, keep conversational follow-up questions separate from standardized ones, and verify uncertain phrasing before moving on.


###


Opalite Health's real-time AI medical interpretation across more than 150 languages and dialects works well as a first-line option for housing, food, and transportation screening when language-specific testing and quality controls are in place. Offer a qualified human interpreter when a patient requests one, when a dialect is unsupported, or when communication difficulties remain unresolved after clarification.


###


Record "declined," "not asked," "unable to complete," and "no need identified" as separate categories in your documentation, and note the language, dialect, administration method, and whether interpretation was used. A patient's refusal to answer does not confirm the absence of a need, and conflating those outcomes distorts your team's picture of unmet needs.


###


Compare screening offers, completed screens, interpreter access, referral acceptance, and completed connections by language, using consistent denominators for each measure. Higher positive-screen rates in some languages may reflect better disclosure; lower rates may reflect missed needs rather than fewer concerns, so review patient feedback and language-specific quality before drawing conclusions.

Check that the draft preserves patient uncertainty, assistance preferences, and referral status exactly as stated; "sometimes worries about food" must not become "no food concerns identified," and a declined referral must not be recorded as "no need identified."
